interpretation: Published depth range is descriptive and is NOT an estimate of clearance today. Do not navigate using this dataset. Dock space, closures, water depth, currents and weather must be verified for a specific vessel and date.

sites.name: Presque Isle, west dock
sites.trail: Julian Bay Trail (0.4 mi) and Anderson Point Trail (1.4 mi)
sites.trailDetail: From the Presque Isle ranger-station area, the short Julian Bay Trail crosses to the beach. Anderson Point takes a longer wooded route between the beach and Presque Isle.
sites.camp: NPS identifies a boardwalk from the west dock to accessible designated campsite #1.
sites.verify: The Presque Isle–Quarry Bay corridor has an earlier bridge washout alert. Confirm specific trail conditions before choosing a longer walk.
sites.label: Beach & accessible camping

sites.name: Presque Isle, east dock
sites.trail: Julian Bay Trail (0.4 mi) and Quarry Bay Trail (3.6 mi)
sites.trailDetail: Start from the Presque Isle visitor area for Julian Bay beach. The 3.6-mile Quarry Bay route crosses interior ground and an area where a meadow path may be difficult to follow.
sites.camp: The NPS lists multiple designated Presque Isle campsites; the separately specified accessible site #1 boardwalk starts at the west dock, not necessarily this east dock.
sites.verify: This shore is not proof that the Quarry Bay trail bridge is repaired or that a vessel has a berth.
sites.label: Short hike & forest crossing

sites.name: Quarry Bay dock
sites.trail: Quarry Trail (1.5 mi) and Quarry Bay Trail (3.6 mi)
sites.trailDetail: Walk the shore toward the old Ashland Brownstone Company quarry, or use the longer connection back toward Presque Isle only after checking current trail conditions.
sites.camp: NPS lists accessible group sites A and B with boardwalk access from the Quarry Bay dock.
sites.verify: Quarry Bay group sites require separate permits and a verified return; the past bridge washout may affect walking to Presque Isle.
sites.label: Quarry history & group camping

sites.name: West dock
sites.trail: Loop Trail (5.2 mi) and Overlook Trail (1.8 mi)
sites.trailDetail: From the dock, reach the loop network. NPS places the main overlook about 3.5 miles from the dock, not just the 1.8-mile length of its spur.
sites.camp: Oak has designated individual and group sites, but not every sandspit campsite is at the west dock; match campsite location to your boat plan.
sites.verify: The reviewed operator listed an Oak overnight shuttle, not a regular same-day hike-and-return service.
sites.label: Long hike & overlooks

sites.name: East Bay dock
sites.trail: Lighthouse Trail (2.0 mi) and Wellisch Cabin Trail (0.6 mi)
sites.trailDetail: Walk north on the lighthouse path or south along the old cabin road. NPS warns lighthouse boardwalks can be slippery when wet.
sites.camp: NPS identifies accessible campsite #3 and accessible group site C by boardwalk from East Bay dock; the agency is correcting older Sand campsite coordinates.
sites.verify: There is no maintained route from East Bay to Lighthouse Bay campsites 4 and 5. Old coordinates and private docks must not be treated as access instructions.
sites.label: Lighthouse & boardwalk camp

sites.name: Light station, west dock
sites.trail: West Bay Trail (1.0 mi) and Sandspit Trail (0.75 mi)
sites.trailDetail: From the lighthouse grounds, reach a west-bay viewpoint or continue through old forest to the southeast sandspit beach.
sites.camp: No designated Raspberry Island campsites and no primitive camping zone. Plan only a day visit.
sites.verify: Confirm whether an advertised lighthouse tour includes landing and lighthouse access for your actual departure.
sites.label: Lighthouse day visit

sites.name: Light station, east dock
sites.trail: West Bay Trail (1.0 mi) and Sandspit Trail (0.75 mi)
sites.trailDetail: Use the light-station trail network for shoreline and historic interpretation. Island tour timing depends on the operator.
sites.camp: No designated campsites on Raspberry Island. This is not a camping itinerary.
sites.verify: Both east and west docks are in the NPS inventory, but neither is a guaranteed public berth or proof of a guided tour.
sites.label: Light station & forest

sites.name: Light station dock
sites.trail: Sandspit / Campsite Trail (1.0 mi) and Lagoon Trail (0.5 mi)
sites.trailDetail: The light-station route leads toward the sandspit. NPS describes the lagoon trail as appearing to stop at a bog and resuming beyond it.
sites.camp: Designated Michigan Island campsite #1 is in the NPS directory, but a permit does not include a tour landing or boat pickup.
sites.verify: A sightseeing cruise that passes a lighthouse is not necessarily a stop ashore. Confirm with the operator.
sites.label: Lighthouses & lagoon

sites.name: East dock
sites.trail: North Trail (0.45 mi), South Trail (0.9 mi), West Trail (1.0 mi)
sites.trailDetail: From the bulletin board by the public dock, go north past campsites 4, 5 and A or south along the shore.
sites.camp: The NPS campsite directory includes designated Rocky sites and group site A; confirm site allocation and permit separately.
sites.verify: Privately occupied land north of Group Site A is not open to visitors.
sites.label: Quiet trails & campsites

sites.name: West dock
sites.trailDetail: A loop from the dock area passes the historic McCloud-Brigham farm landscape and brownstone quarry. NPS places campsites A, 5 and 6 off the near-dock branch.
sites.camp: Campsites 1–4 are southwest of the historic quarry; group site A and sites 5–6 are reached by a separate short branch near dock clearing.
sites.verify: The 5.5-mile route is a significant hike, not an arrival-to-campsite distance or a promise of return time.
sites.label: Quarry heritage loop

sites.name: South landing / marina
sites.trail: Historic Boathouse Trail (1.0 mi) — access blocked
sites.trailDetail: NPS lists the historic trail as an island feature, but the south dock and marina closure means this is NOT a visitor landing or hike recommendation.
sites.camp: Campsites remain marked closed in the researched NPS construction/alert record. No primitive camping is allowed.
sites.verify: Do not land here, treat the historic dock entry as a public berth, or infer reopening from the existence of trail descriptions.
sites.label: Dock closed — no landing
